The user is asking about assessing joint line positions using the contralateral knee as a new approach for planning knee revision surgery. This involves looking at radiographs (X-rays) of the contralateral knee to determine the distance between the fibular head and the joint line, which is considered an important parameter for assessing the joint alignment.

The most precise parameter found in this assessment method is indeed the distance between the fibular head and the joint line. This parameter is correlated with the tibia-first technique used in revision surgery.

Based on these findings, it appears that the contralateral knee can be a useful reference point for assessing joint line positions during knee revision surgery.
